full_judgment: 3. The respondent No. 1 and 2, the Governor, Bangladesh Bank and General Manager, Bangladesh Bank respectively, opposed the rules by filing affidavits-in-opposition and supplementary affidavits-in-opposition denying the allegations and contending inter alia, that the petitioners in total violation of the established practice made payment of Tk. 7,25,400/- and Tk.7,69,144/- against 8 forged bills for which Khulna Police Station Case No. 45 dated 30.09.1993 and 25 dated 19.09.1994 were lodged against them an the police after investigation submitted charge sheets under sections- 409/ 467/ 468/471/ 472 / 190 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and since criminal cases were pending against the petitioners for misappropriation of money through the forged bills, they were placed under suspension by various staff orders in accordance with the provisions of Regulation No. 22(IV) of the Regulation read with Rule 73 of the Bangladesh Service Rules and in the departmental proceeding charges have been framed against them for making payment of Tk. 7,69,144/- and Tk. 7,25,400/- in total Tk. 14,94,544/- against 8 forge bills in violation of section 424 of the Banking Department Manual (BD Manual) and other established practice and the inquiry officer, after enquiry, has also submitted his reports and since criminal cases are pending against the petitioners, Bangladesh Bank did not take any further action in the departmental proceeding and after the disposal of the criminal cases the departmental proceedings will be concluded and sine both the departmental proceedings an criminal proceedings are pending against the petitioners, the writ petitions challenging interim orders of suspension are absolutely misconceived and the remedies of the petitioners, if any, lies with administrative Tribunal and further the petitioners were found guilty in Special Case No. 33 of 1997 and Special Case No. No. 1 of 1997 arising out of the above Khulna P.S. wherein they were convicted and sentenced “দন্ডবিধির ২৮৯/১০৯ ধারামতে ৩(তিন) বৎসর সশ্রম কারাদন্ডে এবং ১.৩০,০০০/-(এক লক্ষ ত্রিশ হাজার) টাকা জরিমানা অনাদায়ে আরো ৯ মাস বিনাশ্রম কারাদন্ড এবং দন্ডবিধির ৪৭১/১০৯ এবং ৪৭২/১০৯ ধারামতে প্রতি ধারায় ৩ বৎসর করিয়া সশ্রম কারাদন্ডে এবং প্রতি ধারায় ৫০০/-(পাঁচশত) টাকা করিয়া জরিমানা অনাদায়ে প্রতি ধারায় আরো ১(এক) মাস করিয়া বিনাশ্রম কারাদন্ডে দন্ডিত করা হইল।” and being aggrieved they filed criminal appeals which were dismissed by the High Court Division and so the present writ petitions are not maintainable. The petitioners filed affidavits-in-reply stating that the above criminal cases and appeals were disposed of after the issuance of the impugned orders of suspension and so the result of those criminal cases and appeals should not have any bearing on the legality of the orders of suspension and that the petitioners filed criminal petitions for leave to appeal against the judgments of the High Court Division.
